title: Trained vs. Untrained: Lower Extremity Pressure Changes
official: Central Blood Volume Shifts in Healthy Adults With Varying Levels of Fitness: Effects on Lung Diffusing Capacity
summary: Research shows that how well oxygen moves from the lungs into the blood (called lung diffusing capacity) is linked to a person's aerobic fitness and endurance training. People who exercise regularly often have different lung and heart responses than people who do not. The exact reasons for these differences are still unclear. This study will test one possible explanation: highly trained people may handle changes in the amount of blood returning to the heart differently than people who are not trained. We want to learn how the blood vessels in the lungs react when the amount of blood entering the heart changes, and how this reaction is affected by fitness level. To do this, we will change how much blood returns to the heart by applying air pressure around the legs, similar to a light vacuum. These changes are expected to be similar to what happens when someone moves from lying down to standing up.

interventions.name: Lower body positive and negative pressure

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18-40 years old.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Severe obesity (body mass index \>35 kg/m2).
* Self-reported blood donation or transfusion in the past 60 days. Large artificial fluctuations in blood volume may impact the findings of the present study.
* Pregnancy. To confirm this, women not using contraception will be given a pregnancy test. Pregnancy presents additional complications and may confound the results of the study; therefore, pregnant women will be excluded.
* Known chronic disease (heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, renal disease).
* Participants with known postural orthostatic tachycardic syndrome or orthostatic hypotension.
* Participants who currently smoke cigarettes (within the last month) or those who have \>1 pack-year smoking history.
* Participants who currently smoke cannabis products (within the last month) or those who have \>1 joint-year cannabis history.
